# Plan: Admin Settings (OAuth + SMTP) & User Invites

## Context

The login page hides OAuth buttons when credentials aren't in ENV vars. Admins need a web UI to configure OAuth and SMTP without touching env files. Additionally, admins should be able to invite users via email link instead of manually setting passwords.

## 1. Settings Model (singleton, single table)

**Create `db/migrate/..._create_settings.rb`:**

```ruby
create_table :settings do |t|
  # OAuth
  t.string :github_client_id
  t.text   :github_client_secret    # encrypted
  t.string :google_client_id
  t.text   :google_client_secret    # encrypted
  # SMTP
  t.string  :smtp_address
  t.integer :smtp_port, default: 587
  t.string  :smtp_username
  t.text    :smtp_password           # encrypted
  t.string  :smtp_authentication, default: "plain"
  t.boolean :smtp_starttls, default: true
  t.string  :smtp_from_address
  t.timestamps
end
```

**Create `app/models/setting.rb`:**
- Singleton pattern: `Setting.instance` → `find_or_create_by(id: 1)`
- `encrypts :github_client_secret, :google_client_secret, :smtp_password`
- Class-level accessors with ENV fallback: `Setting.github_client_id` returns DB value or `ENV["GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"]`
- `github_configured?` / `google_configured?` / `smtp_configured?` helpers
- Secret setters skip blank values (leave-blank-to-keep pattern)
- `smtp_settings` method returns hash for ActionMailer config

## 2. Admin OAuth Settings Page

**Create `app/controllers/admin/settings_controller.rb`:**
- `edit` and `update` actions, Pundit-authorized
- Singular `resource :settings, only: [:edit, :update]` in admin routes

**Create `app/policies/setting_policy.rb`:**
- `def edit? = admin?` / `def update? = admin?`

**Create `app/views/admin/settings/edit.html.erb`:**
- Two card sections: GitHub OAuth, Google OAuth
- Client ID: text field showing current value
- Client Secret: password field, placeholder "Secret is set" or "Enter secret"
- Leave blank = keep current secret

**Modify `config/initializers/omniauth.rb`:**
- Use `setup:` lambda to read credentials from `Setting` at request time (not boot time)

**Modify `app/views/sessions/new.html.erb`:**
- Replace `ENV["GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"].present?` with `Setting.github_configured?`

## 3. Admin SMTP Settings (same page, below OAuth)

**Add to `app/views/admin/settings/edit.html.erb`:**
- SMTP section: address, port, username, password (password field), authentication (select), STARTTLS (checkbox), from address
- "Send Test Email" button (Turbo/fetch POST to `test_email` action)

**Add `test_email` action to `Admin::SettingsController`:**
- Route: `post "settings/test_email"` in admin namespace
- Saves current form params first, then sends test email to current admin's address
- Returns turbo_stream or JSON with success/failure message

**Create `app/mailers/test_mailer.rb`:**
- Simple mailer that sends "SMTP configuration works!" to the admin

**Modify `config/environments/production.rb`:**
- Configure ActionMailer to read SMTP settings from `Setting` dynamically
- Use `ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings` override in an initializer or before_action

**Create `config/initializers/smtp.rb`:**
- Set `ActionMailer::Base.delivery_method = :smtp`
- Use a lazy settings loader or `Mail::SMTP` with dynamic config

## 4. User Invites

**Add to User model (`app/models/user.rb`):**
- `generates_token_for :invite, expires_in: 72.hours` (follows password_reset_token pattern)
- Invite creates user with `status: "pending_approval"`, random secure password

**Create `app/mailers/invite_mailer.rb`:**
- `invite(user)` method, sends link with invite token
- HTML + text templates following `passwords_mailer/reset` pattern

**Create `app/controllers/invites_controller.rb`:**
- `edit` — shows "Set your password" form (finds user by invite token)
- `update` — sets password, activates user (`status: "active"`), signs them in
- Route: `resource :invite, only: [:edit, :update]`

**Modify `app/controllers/admin/users_controller.rb`:**
- Add `invite` action (POST) that creates user + sends invite email
- Or: add "Send Invite" button to user form / users index

**Modify admin users view:**
- Add "Invite User" button/modal (email + name fields)
- Show invite status on users index

{
  "file_path": "/Users/thies/Projects/GitHub/Sandcastle/app/models/setting.rb",
  "content": "class Setting < ApplicationRecord\n  encrypts :github_client_secret, :google_client_secret, :smtp_password\n\n  def self.instance\n    find_or_create_by(id: 1)\n  end\n\n  # --- Class-level accessors with ENV fallback ---\n\n  %i[github_client_id google_client_id].each do |attr|\n    define_singleton_method(attr) do\n      val = instance.send(attr)\n      val.presence || ENV[attr.to_s.upcase]\n    end\n  end\n\n  %i[github_client_secret google_client_secret].each do |attr|\n    define_singleton_method(attr) do\n      val = instance.send(attr)\n      val.presence || ENV[attr.to_s.upcase]\n    end\n  end\n\n  def self.github_configured?\n    github_client_id.present? && github_client_secret.present?\n  end\n\n  def self.google_configured?\n    google_client_id.present? && google_client_secret.present?\n  end\n\n  def self.smtp_configured?\n    instance.smtp_address.present?\n  end\n\n  def self.smtp_from_address\n    val = instance.smtp_from_address\n    val.presence || ENV[\"SMTP_FROM_ADDRESS\"] || \"noreply@example.com\"\n  end\n\n  # Skip blank secret values so \"leave blank to keep\" works\n  %i[github_client_secret google_client_secret smtp_password].each do |attr|\n    define_method(:\"#{attr}=\") do |value|\n      super(value) if value.present?\n    end\n  end\n\n  def smtp_settings\n    return {} unless smtp_address.present?\n\n    settings = {\n      address: smtp_address,\n      port: smtp_port || 587,\n      user_name: smtp_username.presence,\n      password: smtp_password.presence,\n      authentication: smtp_authentication.presence&.to_sym,\n      enable_starttls_auto: smtp_starttls\n    }\n    settings.compact\n  end\nend\n"
}

  "file_path": "/Users/thies/Projects/GitHub/Sandcastle/app/controllers/admin/settings_controller.rb",
  "content": "module Admin\n  class SettingsController < ApplicationController\n    def edit\n      @setting = Setting.instance\n      authorize @setting\n    end\n\n    def update\n      @setting = Setting.instance\n      authorize @setting\n\n      if @setting.update(setting_params)\n        redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, notice: \"Settings saved.\"\n      else\n        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity\n      end\n    end\n\n    def test_email\n      @setting = Setting.instance\n      authorize @setting, :update?\n\n      # Save any pending changes first\n      @setting.update(setting_params) if params[:setting].present?\n\n      if Setting.smtp_configured?\n        begin\n          TestMailer.test(Current.user).deliver_now\n          redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, notice: \"Test email sent to #{Current.user.email_address}.\"\n        rescue => e\n          redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, alert: \"Failed to send test email: #{e.message}\"\n        end\n      else\n        redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, alert: \"SMTP is not configured. Please fill in at least the SMTP address.\"\n      end\n    end\n\n    private\n\n    def setting_params\n      params.expect(setting: [\n        :github_client_id, :github_client_secret,\n        :google_client_id, :google_client_secret,\n        :smtp_address, :smtp_port, :smtp_username, :smtp_password,\n        :smtp_authentication, :smtp_starttls, :smtp_from_address\n      ])\n    end\n  end\nend\n"
}

? \"Set via ENV\" : \"Enter client ID\",\n                class: \"block w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus:outline-blue-600\" %>\n        </div>\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :github_client_secret, \"Client Secret\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.password_field :github_client_secret,\n                placeholder: @setting.github_client_secret.present? %>\n        <p class=\"mt-3 text-sm text-green-600\">GitHub OAuth is active.</p>\n      <% elsif ENV[\"GITHUB_CLIENT_ID\"].present? %>\n        <p class=\"mt-3 text-sm text-gray-500\">Currently using ENV variables.</p>\n      <% end %>\n    </div>\n\n    <%# === Google OAuth === %>\n    <div class=\"rounded-lg border border-gray-200 p-6\">\n      <h2 class=\"text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900 mb-1\">Google OAuth</h2>\n      <p class=\"text-sm text-gray-500 mb-4\">Allow users to sign in with their Google account.</p>\n\n      <div class=\"grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2\">\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :google_client_id, \"Client ID\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.text_field :google_client_id,\n                value: @setting.google_client_id,\n                placeholder: ENV[\"GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID\"].present? ? \"Set via ENV\" : \"Enter client ID\",\n                class: \"block w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus:outline-blue-600\" %>\n        </div>\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :google_client_secret, \"Client Secret\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.password_field :google_client_secret,\n                placeholder: @setting.google_client_secret.present? ? \"Secret is set (leave blank to keep)\" : \"Enter client secret\",\n                class: \"block w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus:outline-blue-600\" %>\n        </div>\n      </div>\n\n      <% if Setting.google_configured? %>\n        <p class=\"mt-3 text-sm text-green-600\">Google OAuth is active.</p>\n      <% elsif ENV[\"GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID\"].present? %>\n        <p class=\"mt-3 text-sm text-gray-500\">Currently using ENV variables.</p>\n      <% end %>\n    </div>\n\n    <%# === SMTP === %>\n    <div class=\"rounded-lg border border-gray-200 p-6\">\n      <h2 class=\"text-lg font-semibold text-gray-900 mb-1\">SMTP / Email</h2>\n      <p class=\"text-sm text-gray-500 mb-4\">Configure outgoing email for password resets and user invites.</p>\n\n      <div class=\"grid gap-4 sm:grid-cols-2\">\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :smtp_address, \"SMTP Server\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.text_field :smtp_address,\n                placeholder: \"smtp.example.com\",\n                class: \"block w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus:outline-blue-600\" %>\n        </div>\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :smtp_port, \"Port\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.number_field :smtp_port,\n                class: \"block w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus:outline-blue-600\" %>\n        </div>\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :smtp_username, \"Username\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.text_field :smtp_username,\n                placeholder: \"user@example.com\",\n                class: \"block w-full rounded-md border border-gray-300 px-3 py-2 text-sm focus:outline-blue-600\" %>\n        </div>\n        <div>\n          <%= form.label :smtp_password, \"Password\", class: \"block text-sm font-medium text-gray-700 mb-1\" %>\n          <%= form.password_field :smtp_password,\n                placeholder: @setting.smtp_password.present? %>\n        <p class=\"mt-3 text-sm text-green-600\">SMTP is configured.</p>\n      <% end %>\n    </div>\n\n    <div class=\"flex items-center gap-3\">\n      <%= form.submit \"Save Settings\", class: \"rounded-md px-3.5 py-2.5 bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-500 text-white text-sm font-medium cursor-pointer\" %>\n\n      <%= button_to \"Send Test Email\", test_email_admin_settings_path, method: :post,\n            form: { id: \"test-email-form\" },\n            class: \"rounded-md px-3.5 py-2.5 border border-gray-300 hover:bg-gray-50 text-sm font-medium cursor-pointer\" %>\n    </div>\n  <% end %>\n</div>\n"

  "content": "Rails.application.config.after_initialize do\n  ActionMailer::Base.delivery_method = :smtp\n\n  # Use a custom delivery method class that reads settings dynamically\n  ActionMailer::Base.class_eval do\n    class_attribute :dynamic_smtp_settings, default: true\n  end\nend\n\n# Interceptor to set SMTP settings per delivery from Setting model\nclass DynamicSmtpInterceptor\n  def self.delivering_email(message)\n    setting = Setting.instance\n    smtp = setting.smtp_settings\n\n    if smtp.present?\n      message.delivery_method(:smtp, smtp)\n    end\n\n    # Set from address if not already set by the mailer\n    from_address = Setting.smtp_from_address\n    if from_address.present? && message.from == [ \"from@example.com\" ]\n      message.from = from_address\n    end\n  end\nend\n\nRails.application.config.after_initialize do\n  ActionMailer::Base.register_interceptor(DynamicSmtpInterceptor)\nend\n"
}

  "content": "require \"test_helper\"\n\nclass SettingTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase\n  setup do\n    Setting.delete_all\n  end\n\n  test \"instance returns singleton\" do\n    setting = Setting.instance\n    assert_equal 1, setting.id\n    assert_equal setting, Setting.instance\n  end\n\n  test \"class-level accessor falls back to ENV\" do\n    ENV[\"GITHUB_CLIENT_ID\"] = \"env_id\"\n    assert_equal \"env_id\", Setting.github_client_id\n  ensure\n    ENV.delete(\"GITHUB_CLIENT_ID\")\n  end\n\n  test \"class-level accessor prefers DB over ENV\" do\n    ENV[\"GITHUB_CLIENT_ID\"] = \"env_id\"\n    Setting.instance.update!(github_client_id: \"db_id\")\n    assert_equal \"db_id\", Setting.github_client_id\n  ensure\n    ENV.delete(\"GITHUB_CLIENT_ID\")\n  end\n\n  test \"github_configured? requires both id and secret\" do\n    refute Setting.github_configured?\n\n    Setting.instance.update!(github_client_id: \"id\")\n    refute Setting.github_configured?\n\n    Setting.instance.update!(github_client_secret: \"secret\")\n    assert Setting.github_configured?\n  end\n\n  test \"google_configured? requires both id and secret\" do\n    refute Setting.google_configured?\n\n    Setting.instance.update!(google_client_id: \"id\", google_client_secret: \"secret\")\n    assert Setting.google_configured?\n  end\n\n  test \"smtp_configured? requires address\" do\n    refute Setting.smtp_configured?\n\n    Setting.instance.update!(smtp_address: \"smtp.example.com\")\n    assert Setting.smtp_configured?\n  end\n\n  test \"blank secret skips update\" do\n    Setting.instance.update!(github_client_secret: \"original\")\n    Setting.instance.update!(github_client_secret: \"\")\n    assert_equal \"original\", Setting.instance.reload.github_client_secret\n  end\n\n  test \"smtp_settings returns hash when configured\" do\n    setting = Setting.instance\n    setting.update!(smtp_address: \"smtp.example.com\", smtp_port: 465, smtp_username: \"user\", smtp_password: \"pass\")\n\n    expected = {\n      address: \"smtp.example.com\",\n      port: 465,\n      user_name: \"user\",\n      password: \"pass\",\n      authentication: :plain,\n      enable_starttls_auto: true\n    }\n    assert_equal expected, setting.smtp_settings\n  end\n\n  test \"smtp_settings returns empty hash when not configured\" do\n    assert_equal({}, Setting.instance.smtp_settings)\n  end\n\n  test \"encrypts secrets\" do\n    Setting.instance.update!(github_client_secret: \"my_secret\")\n    raw = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.select_value(\"SELECT github_client_secret FROM settings WHERE id = 1\")\n    refute_equal \"my_secret\", raw\n    assert_equal \"my_secret\", Setting.instance.github_client_secret\n  end\nend\n"
}

# Postmark SMTP Configuration Details

**Server Address:**
"smtp.postmarkapp.com" for transactional messages or "smtp-broadcasts.postmarkapp.com" for broadcast messages.

**Ports:**
"25, 2525, or 587" are available for connections.

**TLS/SSL Settings:**
"TLS is available via the STARTTLS SMTP extension." This encrypts both credentials and message content during transmission. TLS usage is recommended when possible.

**Authentication Methods:**
Four options are supported:
- **CRAM-MD5** and **DIGEST-MD5**: Protect authentication but leave message content unencrypted without TLS
- **PLAIN**: Sends credentials in clear text; only use with TLS enabled
- **LOGIN**: Similar to PLAIN; provided for compatibility with older clients

**Username and Password:**
You have two options:
1. Use your "Server API Token acts as the username and password" along with a header X-PM-MESSAGE-STREAM for routing
2. Alternatively, use an "SMTP Token" where "The Access Key acts as the username and the Secret Key acts as the password"
```

> AGENT

For Postmark, the admin would enter these values in the Settings page:

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **SMTP Server** | `smtp.postmarkapp.com` |
| **Port** | `587` |
| **Username** | Server API Token (or SMTP Access Key) |
| **Password** | Server API Token (or SMTP Secret Key) |
| **Authentication** | `CRAM-MD5` (recommended) or `Plain` with STARTTLS |
| **STARTTLS** | Checked |
| **From Address** | Your verified sender address in Postmark |

The current implementation already supports all of these settings. The admin just needs to go to `/admin/settings/edit` and fill in the Postmark SMTP details. Want me to add Postmark-specific presets or hints to the settings form, or is the generic SMTP form sufficient?

     2→  class SandboxesController < ApplicationController
     3→    before_action :set_sandbox

     5→    def destroy

     7→      SandboxManager.new.destroy(sandbox: @sandbox)
     8→      redirect_to admin_dashboard_path, notice: "Sandcastle #{@sandbox.name} destroyed"
     9→    end
    10→
    11→    def start
    12→      authorize @sandbox
    13→      SandboxManager.new.start(sandbox: @sandbox)
    14→      redirect_to admin_dashboard_path, notice: "Sandcastle #{@sandbox.name} started"
    15→    end
    16→
    17→    def stop
    18→      authorize @sandbox
    19→      SandboxManager.new.stop(sandbox: @sandbox)
    20→      redirect_to admin_dashboard_path, notice: "Sandcastle #{@sandbox.name} stopped"
    21→    end
    22→
    23→    def stats
    24→      authorize @sandbox
    25→      if @sandbox.status == "running" && @sandbox.container_id.present?
    26→        container = Docker::Container.get(@sandbox.container_id)
    27→        raw = container.stats(stream: false)
    28→
    29→        networks = raw["networks"] || {}
    30→        net_rx = networks.values.sum { |n| n["rx_bytes"] || 0 }
    31→        net_tx = networks.values.sum { |n| n["tx_bytes"] || 0 }
    32→
    33→        blkio = raw.dig("blkio_stats", "io_service_bytes_recursive") || []
    34→        disk_read = blkio.select { |e| e["op"]&.downcase == "read" }.sum { |e| e["value"] || 0 }
    35→        disk_write = blkio.select { |e| e["op"]&.downcase == "write" }.sum { |e| e["value"] || 0 }
    36→
    37→        @stats = {
    38→          cpu_percent: calculate_cpu_percent(raw),
    39→          memory_mb: (raw.dig("memory_stats", "usage") || 0) / 1_048_576.0,
    40→          memory_limit_mb: (raw.dig("memory_stats", "limit") || 0) / 1_048_576.0,
    41→          net_rx: net_rx,
    42→          net_tx: net_tx,
    43→          disk_read: disk_read,
    44→          disk_write: disk_write,
    45→          pids: raw.dig("pids_stats", "current") || 0
    46→        }
    47→      end
    48→
    49→      render partial: "sandbox_stats", locals: { stats: @stats, sandbox: @sandbox }
    50→    rescue Docker::Error::DockerError
    51→      render partial: "sandbox_stats", locals: { stats: nil, sandbox: @sandbox }
    52→    end
    53→
    54→    private
    55→
    56→    def set_sandbox
    57→      @sandbox = Sandbox.active.find(params[:id])
    58→    end
    59→
    60→    def calculate_cpu_percent(stats)
    61→      cpu_delta = stats.dig("cpu_stats", "cpu_usage", "total_usage").to_f -
    62→                  stats.dig("precpu_stats", "cpu_usage", "total_usage").to_f
    63→      system_delta = stats.dig("cpu_stats", "system_cpu_usage").to_f -
    64→                     stats.dig("precpu_stats", "system_cpu_usage").to_f
    65→      num_cpus = stats.dig("cpu_stats", "online_cpus") || 1
    66→
    67→      return 0.0 if system_delta.zero?
    68→      ((cpu_delta / system_delta) * num_cpus * 100.0).round(1)
    69→    end
    70→  end
    71→end
    72→

But wait — the form has `method: :patch`. When `formmethod: "post"` overrides it, does the hidden `_method` field still send `patch`?

> AGENT

Committed. The root cause: the form had a hidden `_method=patch` field, so even with `formmethod="post"` on the button, Rails saw `_method=patch` and routed it as PATCH — which didn't match the `POST test_email` route. Now both buttons submit to the same PATCH update action; the test email button just sends `test_email=1` so the controller knows to also deliver after saving.

Restart your dev server and try again — you should now see either a success message or the actual SMTP error.

The interceptor works — it replaces `localhost:25` with the saved Postmark settings. The flow is:

1. Save button persists SMTP settings to DB
2. Any email delivery triggers `DynamicSmtpInterceptor`
3. Interceptor reads fresh settings from `Setting.instance` and applies them to the message

{
  "file_path": "/Users/thies/Projects/GitHub/Sandcastle/config/initializers/smtp.rb",
  "content": "Rails.application.config.after_initialize do\n  ActionMailer::Base.delivery_method = :smtp\nend\n\n# Interceptor to set SMTP settings per delivery from Setting model\nclass DynamicSmtpInterceptor\n  def self.delivering_email(message)\n    setting = Setting.instance\n    smtp = setting.smtp_settings\n\n    Rails.logger.info \"[SMTP] Interceptor fired for message to=#{message.to.inspect} subject=#{message.subject.inspect}\"\n    Rails.logger.info \"[SMTP] DB settings: #{smtp.reject { |k, _| k == :password }.inspect}\"\n    Rails.logger.info \"[SMTP] smtp_configured?: #{Setting.smtp_configured?}\"\n\n    if smtp.present?\n      message.delivery_method(:smtp, smtp)\n      Rails.logger.info \"[SMTP] Applied dynamic SMTP settings: address=#{smtp[:address]} port=#{smtp[:port]} user=#{smtp[:user_name]}\"\n    else\n      Rails.logger.warn \"[SMTP] No SMTP settings in DB, using defaults (localhost:25)\"\n    end\n\n    # Set from address if not already set by the mailer\n    from_address = Setting.smtp_from_address\n    if from_address.present? && message.from == [ \"from@example.com\" ]\n      message.from = from_address\n      Rails.logger.info \"[SMTP] Overrode from address to #{from_address}\"\n    end\n\n    Rails.logger.info \"[SMTP] Final delivery_method=#{message.delivery_method.class} from=#{message.from.inspect} to=#{message.to.inspect}\"\n  end\nend\n\nRails.application.config.after_initialize do\n  ActionMailer::Base.register_interceptor(DynamicSmtpInterceptor)\nend\n"
}

  "content": "module Admin\n  class SettingsController < BaseController\n    def edit\n      @setting = Setting.instance\n      authorize @setting\n    end\n\n    def update\n      @setting = Setting.instance\n      authorize @setting\n\n      if @setting.update(setting_params)\n        if params[:test_email].present?\n          send_test_email\n        else\n          redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, notice: \"Settings saved.\"\n        end\n      else\n        render :edit, status: :unprocessable_entity\n      end\n    end\n\n    private\n\n    def send_test_email\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] Starting test email flow\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] Setting.smtp_configured? = #{Setting.smtp_configured?}\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] DB smtp_address = #{Setting.instance.smtp_address.inspect}\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] DB smtp_port = #{Setting.instance.smtp_port.inspect}\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] DB smtp_username = #{Setting.instance.smtp_username.inspect}\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] DB smtp_password present? = #{Setting.instance.smtp_password.present?}\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] DB smtp_from_address = #{Setting.instance.smtp_from_address.inspect}\"\n      logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] Recipient = #{Current.user.email_address}\"\n\n      if Setting.smtp_configured?\n        begin\n          logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] Building mail...\"\n          mail = TestMailer.test(Current.user)\n          logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] Mail built: from=#{mail.from.inspect} to=#{mail.to.inspect} delivery_method=#{mail.delivery_method.class}\"\n          logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] Calling deliver_now...\"\n          result = mail.deliver_now\n          logger.info \"[SMTP-TEST] deliver_now returned: #{result.class} message_id=#{result.message_id rescue 'N/A'}\"\n          redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, notice: \"Settings saved. Test email sent to #{Current.user.email_address}.\"\n        rescue => e\n          logger.error \"[SMTP-TEST] DELIVERY FAILED: #{e.class}: #{e.message}\"\n          logger.error \"[SMTP-TEST] Backtrace: #{e.backtrace.first(5).join(\"\\n\")}\"\n          redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, alert: \"Settings saved, but failed to send: #{e.class} - #{e.message}\"\n        end\n      else\n        logger.warn \"[SMTP-TEST] SMTP not configured, skipping send\"\n        redirect_to edit_admin_settings_path, alert: \"Settings saved, but SMTP is not configured. Fill in at least the SMTP address.\"\n      end\n    end\n\n    def setting_params\n      params.expect(setting: [\n        :github_client_id, :github_client_secret,\n        :google_client_id, :google_client_secret,\n        :smtp_address, :smtp_port, :smtp_username, :smtp_password,\n        :smtp_authentication, :smtp_starttls, :smtp_from_address\n      ])\n    end\n  end\nend\n"
}

```
     1→# Plan: Admin Settings (OAuth + SMTP) & User Invites
     2→
     3→## Context
     4→
     5→The login page hides OAuth buttons when credentials aren't in ENV vars. Admins need a web UI to configure OAuth and SMTP without touching env files. Additionally, admins should be able to invite users via email link instead of manually setting passwords.
     6→
     7→## 1. Settings Model (singleton, single table)
     8→
     9→**Create `db/migrate/..._create_settings.rb`:**
    10→
    11→```ruby
    12→create_table :settings do |t|
    13→  # OAuth
    14→  t.string :github_client_id
    15→  t.text   :github_client_secret    # encrypted
    16→  t.string :google_client_id
    17→  t.text   :google_client_secret    # encrypted
    18→  # SMTP
    19→  t.string  :smtp_address
    20→  t.integer :smtp_port, default: 587
    21→  t.string  :smtp_username
    22→  t.text    :smtp_password           # encrypted
    23→  t.string  :smtp_authentication, default: "plain"
    24→  t.boolean :smtp_starttls, default: true
    25→  t.string  :smtp_from_address
    26→  t.timestamps
    27→end
    28→```
    29→
    30→**Create `app/models/setting.rb`:**
    31→- Singleton pattern: `Setting.instance` → `find_or_create_by(id: 1)`
    32→- `encrypts :github_client_secret, :google_client_secret, :smtp_password`
    33→- Class-level accessors with ENV fallback: `Setting.github_client_id` returns DB value or `ENV["GITHUB_CLIENT_ID"]`
    34→- `github_configured?` / `google_configured?` / `smtp_configured?` helpers
    35→- Secret setters skip blank values (leave-blank-to-keep pattern)
    36→- `smtp_settings` method returns hash for ActionMailer config
    37→
    38→## 2. Admin OAuth Settings Page
    39→
    40→**Create `app/controllers/admin/settings_controller.rb`:**
    41→- `edit` and `update` actions, Pundit-authorized

## Sandcastle Codebase Exploration Report

I've thoroughly explored the Sandcastle codebase to understand the sandbox architecture, SSH setup, networking topology, and UI rendering. Here are my detailed findings:

### 1. **Sandbox Creation & SSH Setup**

**File:** `app/services/sandbox_manager.rb` (lines 7-58)

Sandbox creation flow:
- **DB model creation**: Creates a `Sandbox` record with status `pending`
- **Image pull**: Ensures the sandbox image exists locally
- **Mount directory setup**: Creates `/data/users/{username}/home` and persistent volumes as needed
- **Docker container creation** via `docker-api` gem:
  - Container runtime: `sysbox-runc` (falls back to `runc` if unavailable)
  - Environment variables passed: `SANDCASTLE_USER` and `SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY` (public key)
  - SSH port binding: Maps container port 22 to host port in range 2201-2299
  - Volume binds:
    - User home: `{SANDCASTLE_DATA_DIR}/users/{username}/home:/home/{username}`
    - Persistent volume (if enabled): `{DATA_DIR}/sandboxes/{full_name}/vol:/workspace`
    - Custom data path (if provided): User-provided directory mapped to `/data`
  - Restart policy: `unless-stopped`

**SSH entrypoint setup:**

**File:** `images/sandbox/entrypoint.sh`

The entrypoint script (running in the container on startup):
1. Creates the user account (from `SANDCASTLE_USER` env var)
2. Grants sudo access without password
3. Installs SSH public key from `SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY` to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`
4. Generates SSH host keys (`ssh-keygen -A`)
5. Starts Docker daemon in background (if Sysbox available)
   - Matches inner Docker MTU to container's eth0 to avoid packet fragmentation
   - Waits up to 30 seconds for dockerd to be ready
6. Starts SSH daemon in foreground (`sshd -D -e`)

**Key detail:** SSH uses **key-only authentication** (no passwords). Both the entrypoint.sh and sandbox Dockerfile confirm `PasswordAuthentication no`.

---

### 2. **SSH Port Assignment & Mapping**

**File:** `app/models/sandbox.rb` (lines 5, 39-45)

**Port range:** 2201-2299 (99 available ports)

**Assignment mechanism:**
- `before_validation :assign_ssh_port` on create
- Queries used ports from non-destroyed sandboxes
- Assigns first available port from the range
- Raises error if all ports exhausted
- Ports are freed when sandboxes are destroyed (status: "destroyed")

**Network binding:**
- Container port 22 (SSH daemon inside sandbox) → Host port (2201-2299)
- This is configured in `SandboxManager.create()` via Docker PortBindings:
  ```ruby
  "PortBindings" => { "22/tcp" => [ { "HostPort" => sandbox.ssh_port.to_s } ] }
  ```
- The Docker host itself needs to be reachable (typically via `SANDCASTLE_HOST` env var)

---

### 3. **Sandbox Model - Available Fields/Data**

**File:** `app/models/sandbox.rb`

Key fields in the Sandbox model:
- `id` — Primary key
- `user_id` — Foreign key to User
- `name` — Sandbox name (lowercase alphanumeric, validated unique per user)
- `full_name` — Computed: `{user.name}-{name}` (Docker container name)
- `container_id` — Docker container ID (set after creation)
- `ssh_port` — Assigned port (2201-2299)
- `status` — State: "pending", "running", "stopped", "destroyed"
- `image` — Docker image URL (defaults to `ghcr.io/thieso2/sandcastle-sandbox:latest`)
- `persistent_volume` — Boolean flag
- `volume_path` — Full path if persistent (e.g., `/data/sandboxes/{full_name}/vol`)
- `mount_home` — Boolean: mount user's home directory
- `data_path` — Custom data directory path
- `temporary` — Boolean: marks as temporary (auto-removes instead of destroy)
- `tailscale` — Boolean: connected to Tailscale sidecar
- `created_at`, `updated_at` — Timestamps
- Has many `routes` (for HTTP proxying to sandbox services)

---

### 4. **Dashboard UI - Sandbox Card Rendering**

**Files:** `app/views/dashboard/_sandbox.html.erb` (user view), `app/views/admin/dashboard/_sandbox.html.erb` (admin view)

**Card structure (2 lines):**

**Line 1 — Status, name, and feature pills:**
- **Status indicator**: Colored dot
  - Green: running
  - Yellow: stopped
  - Blue pulsing: pending
  - Gray: destroyed
- **Name**: `<span class="font-mono">` — displayed in monospace
- **Feature pills** (badges):
  - `temp` — amber badge if temporary
  - `home` — blue badge if home mounted (with house icon)
  - `data:{path}` — blue badge if custom data path
  - `volume` — blue badge if persistent volume enabled
  - `Tailscale` — purple badge if connected to Tailscale
  - **Route links** — green badges with external link icon, clickable to route URL
- **Action buttons** (right side):
  - If temporary: "Remove" button only
  - If running: "Stop" and "Destroy" buttons
  - If stopped: "Start" and "Destroy" buttons

**Line 2 — Metadata and stats:**
- **Left side**: Container details
  - Container ID (first 12 chars) in monospace
  - Image name (with `ghcr.io/thieso2/` prefix removed)
  - Creation time (e.g., "Created 2 hours ago")
  - Running/stopped duration
- **Right side**: Live stats (via Turbo Frame)
  - If running, loads stats lazily via `turbo_frame_tag`
  - Shows CPU/memory usage for running containers

**Rendering context:**
- User dashboard: Only shows user's own sandboxes
- Admin dashboard: Shows all sandboxes with username badge for each

---

### 5. **docker-compose.local.yml Networking**

**File:** `docker-compose.local.yml`

**Services:**
- `postgres` — PostgreSQL database
- `init-data` — Setup /data volume permissions
- `web` — Rails web container
- `migrate` — Runs migrations before web starts

**Networking setup:**
- **Docker socket access**: `web` container has:
  - Volume mount: `/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock`
  - `group_add: ["${DOCKER_GID:-0}"]` — Access to Docker group on host
  - This allows Rails to use `docker-api` gem to control sandbox containers
  
- **Data volume**: `sandcastle-data:/data`
  - Shared with the host at `/data` (or configured `SANDCASTLE_DATA_DIR`)
  - Used for user homes, persistent volumes, Tailscale state directories

- **Communication with sandboxes**:
  - Via Docker API (not direct network calls)
  - Sandboxes run on the host Docker daemon (not inside web container)
  - SSH access is port-mapped on the host (2201-2299)

---

### 6. **Tailscale Sidecar Networking**

**File:** `app/services/tailscale_manager.rb`

**Architecture:**

Per-user Tailscale sidecar setup:
- **Sidecar container**: `sc-ts-{username}` (runs `tailscale/tailscale:latest`)
- **Bridge network**: `sc-ts-net-{username}` with per-user subnet (e.g., `172.{100+uid}.0.0/24`)
- **State persistence**: `/data/users/{username}/tailscale`

**Key features:**
1. **Two authentication flows:**
   - **Auth key flow** (legacy `enable`): Uses `TS_AUTHKEY` env var with containerboot entrypoint
   - **Interactive login flow** (`start_login` → `check_login`): 
     - Runs tailscaled directly (custom entrypoint)
     - Executes `tailscale up --reset --advertise-routes=<subnet> --timeout=120s` in background
     - Polls `tailscale status --json` to detect auth completion
     - User must click browser link to authenticate

2. **Sandbox integration:**
   - When sandbox is created with Tailscale enabled:
     - `TailscaleManager.connect_sandbox()` connects sandbox container to the bridge network
     - Sandbox gets an IP on the per-user subnet (e.g., `172.101.0.0/24`)
     - Sidecar advertises subnet routes to the Tailscale network
   - Sandboxes are reachable from the user's Tailnet via their Tailscale IP
   - SSH port becomes 22 (not 2201-2299) when using Tailscale

3. **User state field:**
   - `tailscale_state`: "disabled" → "pending" (during login) → "enabled"
   - `tailscale_auto_connect`: Auto-joins new sandboxes to bridge network

4. **Networking details:**
   - Sidecar capabilities: `NET_ADMIN`, `SYS_MODULE`
   - Device access: `/dev/net/tun` (TUN device for Tailscale)
   - Sysctl: `net.ipv4.ip_forward=1` (subnet advertisement)

---

### 7. **Overall Networking Topology**

---

### Key Insights for WeTTY Integration

**Connection options for WeTTY to SSH into sandboxes:**

1. **Host port binding** (if WeTTY is inside web container):
   - WeTTY would SSH to Docker host via `/var/run/docker.sock`
   - Query `docker inspect <container>` to get the Docker host's SANDCASTLE_HOST
   - SSH to `{SANDCASTLE_HOST}:{ssh_port}` with the user's private key

2. **Docker network** (if WeTTY is on same Docker host):
   - WeTTY can reach sandbox container by name: `{user}-{name}`
   - SSH to `{user}-{name}:22` directly
   - Requires WeTTY container to be on the same Docker network or have DNS resolution

3. **Tailscale network** (if user has Tailscale enabled):
   - WeTTY queries sandbox's `tailscale_ip` from database
   - SSH to `tailscale_ip:22` (no port remapping)
   - More secure and works over WireGuard tunnel

**Critical constraint for WeTTY container:**
- Must either:
  - Be on the host Docker network (to reach 2201-2299 via localhost)
  - OR be placed on the same bridge network as sandboxes it connects to
  - OR use Tailscale IPs if available

---

This completes the comprehensive exploration of the Sandcastle codebase. The architecture is clean: Docker + Sysbox for isolation, SSH for terminal access (port-mapped 2201-2299), with optional Tailscale for encrypted networking. The UI correctly reflects all sandbox states and features through badge indicators.

### 6. **SSH Key Injection in SandboxManager** (`app/services/sandbox_manager.rb`)

**Current Flow (lines 7-58):**

1. **User SSH Public Key Storage:**
   - Stored in `User` model as `ssh_public_key` (text column)
   - Set during user creation or account setup

2. **Container Creation (`create` method):**
   ```ruby
   Docker::Container.create(
     "name" => sandbox.full_name,
     "Env" => [
       "SANDCASTLE_USER=#{user.name}",
       "SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY=#{user.ssh_public_key}"  # ← Injected as env var
     ],
     ...
   )
   ```

3. **Key Injection Process:**
   - SSH public key passed as `SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY` environment variable to container
   - Container's entrypoint reads this and writes to `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`
   - Only one key is authorized per user (static, persistent)

4. **Also Used in `restore` method (lines 183-234):**
   - Same pattern when restoring from snapshot

**File:** `/Users/thies/Projects/GitHub/Sandcastle/app/services/sandbox_manager.rb` (lines 7-58, 183-234)

### 7. **SSH Key Injection in Sandbox Image** (`images/sandbox/entrypoint.sh`)

**Key Setup (lines 14-22):**
```bash
if [ -n "$SSH_KEY" ]; then
    SSH_DIR="/home/$USERNAME/.ssh"
    mkdir -p "$SSH_DIR"
    echo "$SSH_KEY" > "$SSH_DIR/authorized_keys"
    chmod 700 "$SSH_DIR"
    chmod 600 "$SSH_DIR/authorized_keys"
    chown -R "$USERNAME:$USERNAME" "$SSH_DIR"
fi
```

**Entrypoint Flow:**
1. Creates user if not exists (line 8)
2. Sets up SSH authorized_keys from `SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY` env var
3. Starts Docker daemon (lines 44-57)
4. Starts SSH daemon: `exec /usr/sbin/sshd -D -e` (line 60)

**SSH Configuration (`Dockerfile` lines 44-49):**
- Key-only auth enabled
- Password auth disabled
- Root login disabled

### 8. **Connection Info Endpoint** (`app/controllers/api/sandboxes_controller.rb` + `app/services/sandbox_manager.rb`)

**API Response (lines 59-62 in controller):**
```ruby
def connect
  info = SandboxManager.new.connect_info(sandbox: @sandbox)
  render json: info
end
```

**SandboxManager#connect_info (lines 236-257):**
```ruby
def connect_info(sandbox:)
  host = ENV.fetch("SANDCASTLE_HOST", "localhost")
  user = sandbox.user.name
  info = {
    host: host,
    port: sandbox.ssh_port,
    user: user,
    command: sandbox.connect_command(host: host)
  }

  if sandbox.tailscale?
    ts_ip = TailscaleManager.new.sandbox_tailscale_ip(sandbox: sandbox)
    if ts_ip.present?
      info[:host] = ts_ip
      info[:port] = 22
      info[:command] = "ssh #{user}@#{ts_ip}"
      info[:tailscale_ip] = ts_ip
    end
  end

  info
end
```

**Returns JSON:**
```json
{
  "host": "sandcastle.example.com",
  "port": 2201,
  "user": "thies",
  "command": "ssh -p 2201 thies@sandcastle.example.com",
  "tailscale_ip": "100.x.x.x"  // if tailscale enabled
}
```

## Summary for WeTTY Terminal Integration

**Key Points for Implementation:**

1. **UI Integration Point:** Add terminal icon button to line 35-52 in `/app/views/dashboard/_sandbox.html.erb` alongside Start/Stop/Destroy buttons. Use Heroicons terminal icon with same badge styling.

2. **SSH Key Generation Strategy:**
   - Current: Static user SSH key passed to container via `SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY` env var
   - **For WeTTY:** Need per-session temporary SSH keys (separate from user's main key)
   - Can pass additional env var like `WETTY_SSH_KEY` alongside `SANDCASTLE_SSH_KEY` during container creation
   - Or generate WeTTY key on-the-fly and insert into container via API before starting WeTTY

3. **Key Injection Methods:**
   - Option A: Add to `SandboxManager.create()` method, pass as separate env var
   - Option B: POST to `/api/sandboxes/:id/connect` endpoint and generate ephemeral key, return WeTTY connection details
   - Option C: Create new `/api/sandboxes/:id/wetty_session` endpoint that generates temporary key and returns WeTTY URL

4. **Container Management:** Key is injected into container entrypoint via Docker env vars - clean separation of concerns.

5. **Routes Available:** Can add new route like `post :wetty_session` to API sandboxes resource for generating session-specific keys.
